messages:
mira: quick heads up — ran the contract fuzzer against int4-v2 on the funcall path, found ~120 schema violations in 1k samples :eyes:
jon: ugh, any patterns?
mira: most are small — reordered object keys + dangling commas + occasionally an extra stray null in the tool args
anya: reordered keys shouldn't break our parser tho, we use a tolerant loader?
mira: right but two things stack: (1) when streaming + batching we sometimes cut mid-token and glue suffixes differently, (2) the retry actor can re-emit a previously truncated tail which ends up duplicating a key -> downstream strict validators choke
kevin: can you paste a minimal repro?
mira: pasted a couple examples from the fuzzer run:

```
fuzzer-bot: sample_472.json
{"tool":"update_user","args":{"id":123,"email":null,,"display":"alex"}}
```

```
fuzzer-bot: sample_489.json
{"tool":"update_user","args":{"display":"alex","id":123}\n}\n
```

mira: notice the extra comma and the mismatched brace split across stream chunks
jon: `extra comma` is from the model output — are we seeing this only on int4-v2? or earlier floats too?
mira: spike on int4-v2 and also when batch_size>1. float FP16 didn't show same duplicates in 5k samples
anya: telemetry? any correlation with latency or retries?
ci-bot: telemetry snapshot: funcall.parse_errors increased 11x during the run window; retry_count per request average 1.8 -> 2.3
kevin: suspect: quantization changed tokenization alignment so EOS/commas land on different subtoken boundaries; with continuous batching the runtime's chunking causes suffix reassembly edge cases
anya: could be. I saw earlier a similar bug but that was fixed by adding an explicit JSON wrapper during streaming (prefix + \"BEGIN_JSON\" / suffix).
mira: quick experiments: adding a sentinel token before the json body dropped parse errors by ~70% in a small sample
jon: good signal. What's the risk of wrapper? breaks some customers relying on raw outputs
kevin: we can make wrapper a canary for int4-v2 only and auto-strip for dev-only clients. Also add post-output sanitizer to remove trailing commas and run quick NDJSON-lint heuristics before handing to parser
anya: quick mitigation steps then: (1) canary wrapper in canary pool (int4-v2, batch>1), (2) add lightweight sanitizer, (3) fail-open with best-effort parse plus logging when sanitizer altered output
mira: will open ticket with repro samples and attach the fuzzer corpus. Also schedule a 30m triage call
jon: assign to kevin for runtime change, anya for sanitizer + validator changes
kevin: on it. I'll spin up a small canary job and run the fuzzer corpus overnight
ci-bot: ticket created: INF-6421 — "stream-reassembly-json-floss-on-quant-canary"
fuzzer-bot: corpus uploaded to s3://redwood-fuzz/int4-v2/4309000001/ with 1.2k samples
anya: nice. one more ask: add a telemetry gauge for "sanitizer_mutations" so we can monitor if sanitizer becomes a crutch
mira: agreed. I'll add to the ticket and the triage agenda
jon: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
